Surah At-Talaq is Madani. [Ibn al-Đarīs, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: Surat al-Talaq was revealed in Madinah. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/188.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ He addressed the Prophet (ﷺ) and then addressed his community, because he is the foremost leader, so the address to all is included with him.

It has also been said: its meaning is, "O Prophet, tell your community: when you (plural) divorce women," meaning when you intend to divorce them, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 98], meaning when you intend to recite.

﴿Divorce them at their waiting period﴾ meaning at their purity, with that which they reckon as their waiting period. Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn ʿUmar used to recite: "Divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period." This verse was revealed concerning ʿAbdullah [ibn ʿUmar], who had divorced his wife during her menstruation. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Tafsir of Surat al-Talaq: 8/653.]

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih informed us: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Musʿab informed us, from Malik [from Nafiʿ], from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar, that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and he said: "Order him to take her back, then let him keep her until she becomes pure, then she menstruates, then [she becomes pure]. Then, if he wishes, he may keep her afterwards, and if he wishes, he may divorce her before he touches her. That is the waiting period which Allah commanded for women to be divorced in." [Narrated by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta, in Divorce, chapter on what has come concerning the periods, the waiting period of divorce and the divorce of a menstruating woman: 2/576; al-Bukhari in Divorce, chapter on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: (O Prophet, when you divorce women): 9/345-346; Muslim in Divorce, chapter on the prohibition of divorcing a menstruating woman without her consent, no. 1471: 2/1093; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/202.]

Salim narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: "Order him to take her back, then let him divorce her while she is pure or pregnant." [Narrated by Muslim in Divorce, chapter on the prohibition of divorcing a menstruating woman without her consent, no. 1471: 2/1095.]

Yunus ibn Jubayr and Anas ibn Sirin also narrated it from Ibn ʿUmar, but they did not say "then she menstruates, then she becomes pure." [Ibid.]

ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabiʿ informed us: al-Shafiʿi informed us: Muslim and Saʿid ibn Salim informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ayman, the freedman of ʿAzzah, asking ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar, while Abu al-Zubayr was listening: "What is your view concerning a man who divorced his wife while she was menstruating?" Ibn ʿUmar said: "ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar divorced his wife while she was menstruating, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Order him to take her back, and when she becomes pure, let him either divorce or keep her.'" Ibn ʿUmar said: "And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period, or for their waiting period﴾." Al-Shafiʿi was uncertain.

Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated it from Ibn Jurayj, and said: Ibn ʿUmar said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period﴾." [Narrated by al-Shafiʿi: 2/33 (Tartib al-Musnad) and Muslim in Divorce, no. 1471: 2/1098.]

Know that divorce during menstruation and postpartum bleeding is an innovation (bid'ah) (a matter introduced in the religion without basis), and likewise in the purity in which he had intercourse with her, due to the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "or, if he wishes, he may divorce her before he touches her."

The lawful divorce (al-talaq al-sunni) (the divorce in accordance with the Sunnah) is that he divorces her in a purity in which he has not had intercourse with her. This applies to a woman whose waiting period is by menstrual cycles.

As for divorcing a woman not yet consummated during menstruation, or divorcing a young girl who has never menstruated, or a woman past menopause after intercourse, or a pregnant woman after intercourse, or in a state of seeing blood, it is not an innovation. There is neither Sunnah nor innovation in the divorce of these, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "then let him divorce her while she is pure or pregnant."

Khul' (divorce by wife's request for compensation) during menstruation, or in a purity in which he had intercourse with her, is not an innovation, because the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted Thabit ibn Qays to khul' his wife without inquiring into her condition. Had it not been permissible in all circumstances, it would have been necessary to inquire about her condition.

If he divorces his wife during menstruation, or in a purity in which he had intercourse with her, deliberately, he sins against Allah, the Exalted, but the divorce takes effect, because the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered Ibn ʿUmar to take her back. Had the divorce not taken effect, he would not have ordered taking her back. If he takes her back during menstruation, it is permissible to divorce her in the purity that follows that menstruation, before touching her, as narrated by Yunus ibn Jubayr and Anas ibn Sirin from Ibn ʿUmar.

As for what Nafiʿ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar: "then let him keep her until she becomes pure, then she menstruates, then she becomes pure," this is a recommendation: he recommended delaying the divorce until the second purity, so that his taking her back is not for the sake of divorce, just as marriage for the sake of divorce is disliked.

There is no innovation in pronouncing the three divorces together according to some scholars, so that if he divorces his wife three times in a state of purity, it is not an innovation. This is the view of al-Shafiʿi and Ahmad. Others held that it is an innovation, and this is the view of Malik and the companions of opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y) (the Hanafi jurists).

The saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And count the waiting period﴾, meaning the number of its periods; preserve them. It was said: He commanded counting the waiting period so that divorce is spread over the periods when he wishes to divorce three times. It was also said: so that one knows the remaining time for the right of return and attends to matters of maintenance and lodging.

﴿And fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses﴾ He meant: if the dwelling in which he divorced her belongs to the husband, it is not lawful for him to expel her from it. ﴿Nor should they leave﴾, and it is not lawful for her to leave until her waiting period has ended. If she leaves without necessity or need, she sins. If a necessity arises, even if she fears collapse or drowning, she may leave for another dwelling. Likewise, if she has a need, such as selling yarn or buying cotton, it is permissible for her to go out by day but not by night. When men were martyred at Uhud, their wives said: "We feel lonely in our houses," so the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted them to gather at one another's homes, and when it was time to sleep, each woman returned to her own house. [Narrated by al-Shafiʿi in al-Umm: 5/217, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 7/436, from Mujahid as a mursal report, and its chain of narrators is trustworthy; and ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 7/36. See Talkhis al-Habir: 3/240.] The Prophet (ﷺ) also permitted the maternal aunt of Jabir, whose husband had divorced her, to go out to harvest her date palms. [Narrated by Muslim in Divorce, chapter on the permissibility of an irrevocably divorced or widowed woman going out during the day for her need, no. 1483: 3/1121.]

If the waiting period falls due during travel, she observes it while traveling and while returning; and the Bedouin woman observes it wherever her people settle during the waiting period, because movement for them is in place of residence for one who resides.

His saying: ﴿except that they commit a clear indecency﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "The clear indecency" is that she behaves badly toward her husband's family, so it becomes lawful to expel her. [Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 6/323, and al-Tabari: 28/133-134. al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/193 to Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Rahawayh, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh. al-Shafiʿi and al-Bayhaqi also narrated it; see Talkhis al-Habir: 3/241.]

A group said: by indecency is meant adultery, so she is taken out to have the prescribed punishment (hadd) carried out on her, and then she is returned to her home. This is narrated from Ibn Masʿud. [See al-Tabari: 28/134; Ibn Kathir: 4/379.]

Qatadah said: its meaning is that he divorces her because of her rebellion (nushuz), so she may move away from her husband's house, and "indecency" means rebellion.

Ibn ʿUmar and al-Suddi said: her leaving before the end of the waiting period is indecency. [Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/134. See al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/282.]

﴿Those are the limits of Allah﴾, meaning what has been mentioned of the Sunnah of divorce and what follows it. ﴿Whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾ — He places in the husband's heart the desire to take her back after one or two divorces. This indicates that it is preferable to separate the divorces and not to pronounce three at once, so that if he regrets, he is able to take her back.

﴿فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾ (When they reach their term), i.e., they draw near to the end of their waiting period (ʿiddah). ﴿فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾ (then retain them), i.e., take them back (rajʿah). ﴿بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ فَارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ (in kindness or part from them in kindness), i.e., leave them until their waiting period ends, whereupon they become separated from you. ﴿وَأَشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ﴾ (and call to witness two just men from among you), concerning the taking back and the separation. He commanded calling witnesses both for the taking back and for the divorce.

﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الشَّهَادَةَ﴾ (And establish the testimony), O witnesses, ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ (for Allah).

﴿ذَلِكُمْ يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا﴾ (That is what he is admonished with, whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out). ʿIkrimah, al-Shaʿbi and al-Ḍaḥḥak said: "And whoever fears Allah and divorces according to the Sunnah, He will make for him a way out to the taking back" [[See: al-Ṭabari: 28/138.]].

Most of the exegetes said: it was revealed concerning ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿi. The polytheists took captive his son named Mālik, so he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the enemy has taken my son captive," and he also complained to him of poverty. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Fear Allah, be patient, and recite much: there is no power and no strength except with Allah." The man did so, and while he was in his house, his son came to him, the enemy having been careless about him, and he had seized camels and brought them to his father [[See: al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, pp. 502–503; Ibn Kathir: 4/381.]].

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The enemy was careless about him, so he drove off their sheep, and brought them to his father, and they were four thousand sheep. Then it was revealed: 'And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out'" [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/197 to Ibn Mardawayh. See also al-Ṭabari: 28/138; Ibn Kathir: 4/381.]] concerning his son.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 65, verse 3:

﴿And He provides for him from where he does not expect.﴾ That is what he drove of sheep.

Muqatil said: He acquired sheep and goods, then returned to his father. His father went to the Prophet ﷺ, informed him of the matter, and asked him: "Is it lawful for him to eat what his son brought?" The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Yes." And Allah revealed this verse.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out" means that he knows it comes from Allah and that Allah is his provider.

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: "He will make for him a way out" from every matter that is constricted upon people.

Abu al-Aliyah said: "A way out" from every hardship.

Al-Hasan said: "A way out" from what He has forbidden him.

﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him.﴾ Whoever fears Allah regarding what befalls him, He will suffice him in what concerns him.

It has been related to us that the Prophet ﷺ said: "If you truly relied upon Allah as He deserves, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter on what has come regarding asceticism in this world, 7/8, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith which we only know from this route." And Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, chapter on tawakkul and certainty, no. (4164), 2/1394; Imam Ahmad, 1/30; al-Tayalisi in his Musnad p. (11), and al-Hakim authenticated it, 4/318, and al-Dhahabi agreed; Ibn Hibban p. (633) from Mawarid al-Dhama'an; Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Kitab al-Tawakkul no. (1); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 14/301. See Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah no. (310).]

﴿Indeed, Allah accomplishes His command.﴾ Talhah ibn Musarrif and Hafs from Asim read "balighu amrih" with the genitive construction (idafah); the others read "balighun" with tanwin [omitted in "a"] "amrahu" in the accusative, meaning: He carries out His command, executing His decree in His creation.

﴿Allah has already set a measure for everything.﴾ That is, He has set for everything, whether hardship or ease, a term at which it ends.

Masruq said: Regarding this verse, "Indeed, Allah accomplishes His command": whether one relies upon Him or does not rely upon Him, the one who relies upon Him has his sins expiated from him and his reward magnified.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 65, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation﴾, so that you do not expect them to menstruate, ﴿if you are in doubt﴾, meaning if you are uncertain and do not know what their 'iddah (waiting period) is, ﴿then their 'iddah is three months﴾.

Muqatil said: When the verse "And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods" [al-Baqarah: 228] was revealed, Khallad ibn al-Nu'man ibn Qays al-Ansari said: "O Messenger of God, what is the 'iddah of the woman who no longer menstruates, the one who has not yet menstruated, and the pregnant woman?" So God revealed: "And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation" [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 503. And see Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Shafi'i: 1/324.]], meaning the postmenopausal women (al-qawa'id), who have ceased menstruating. "If you are in doubt" means if you are uncertain about their ruling. "Then their 'iddah is three months."

﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾, meaning the young girls who have not yet menstruated, their 'iddah is also three months. As for the young woman who used to menstruate but her menstruation ceased before she reached the age of those who despair of menstruation: most scholars held that her 'iddah does not end until the blood returns to her, so that she observes three menstrual cycles (qur'), or she reaches the age of those who despair of menstruation, whereupon she observes three months. This is the view of Uthman, Ali, Zayd ibn Thabit and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and Ata' said likewise. Al-Shafi'i and the Ashab al-Ra'y (the proponents of opinion) also held this view.

It is related from Umar that she waits nine months; if she does not menstruate, she then observes three months. This is also the view of Malik. Al-Hasan said: she waits a year; if she does not menstruate, she then observes three months. All of this concerns the 'iddah of divorce.

As for the widow, her 'iddah is four months and ten days, whether she is one who menstruates or not.

As for the pregnant woman, her 'iddah ends with the delivery of the child, whether her husband divorced her or died leaving her, based on God's saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for those with children, their term is that they deliver their burden﴾.

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us, who said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us, who said: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us, who said: al-Rabi' informed us, who said: al-Shafi'i informed us, who said: Sufyan informed us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd Allah [ibn Abd Allah] [[Omitted from "b".]], on the authority of his father: that Subay'a bint al-Harith gave birth a few nights after her husband's death. Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak passed by her and said: "You have adorned yourself for suitors! Her 'iddah is four months and ten days." Subay'a mentioned this to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: "Abu al-Sanabil lied, or: it is not as Abu al-Sanabil said. You have been released; so marry." [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i: 2/51-52 (Tartib al-Musnad), and al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter: "And for those with children, their term is that they deliver their burden," 9/469-470, and Muslim in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on the expiry of the 'iddah of a widow and others by delivery of the child, no. 1484, 2/1122. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/304.]]

﴿And whoever fears God, He will make for him ease in his affair﴾, meaning He will make the affairs of this world and the Hereafter easy for him.

﴿That﴾, meaning the rulings mentioned, ﴿is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears Allah, He will remove his misdeeds from him and magnify his reward﴾.

﴿Let them dwell﴾, meaning the women you have divorced, ﴿in the same dwellings where you dwell﴾. "Min" (from) is a *ṣilah* (an extraneous particle), so the meaning is: let them dwell where you dwell. ﴿According to your means﴾, meaning your wealth and capacity. That is, if the husband is well-off, he should provide generously for her in lodging and maintenance, and if he is poor, then according to his capacity. ﴿And do not harm them﴾, meaning do not hurt them, ﴿to restrict them﴾ in their dwellings so that they are forced to leave. ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth﴾, meaning until they leave their waiting period (*'iddah*).

Know that a woman in a revocable *'iddah* is entitled from her husband to maintenance (*nafaqah*) and lodging (*sukna*) for as long as she is in the *'iddah*. By lodging we mean the cost of housing. If the house in which he divorced her belongs to the husband, he must leave and vacate the house for her for the duration of her *'iddah*. If it is rented, then the rent is the husband's obligation. If it is a loan (*'ariyah*) and the lender withdraws it, then he must rent a house for her to live in.

As for a woman in an irrevocable *'iddah* (*al-mu'taddah al-ba'innah*), whether by *khul'* (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation), by three divorces, or by *li'an* (mutual oath-cursing), she is entitled to lodging, whether she is pregnant or not, according to the majority of scholars.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "She has no lodging unless she is pregnant." This is also the view of al-Hasan, 'Ata' and al-Sha'bi.

They differed regarding her maintenance. One group held that she has no maintenance unless she is pregnant. This is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the view of al-Hasan, 'Ata' and al-Sha'bi, and al-Shafi'i and Ahmad also held it. [Note: see al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 6/507, 508.]

Others held that it is obligatory in every case. This is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, and it is the view of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. al-Thawri and the *Ashab al-Ra'y* (People of Opinion) also held it.

The apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that she is not entitled to it unless she is pregnant, because Allah the Exalted said: "And if they are pregnant, then spend on them."

The evidence from the Sunnah is what follows:

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid, client of al-Aswad ibn Sufyan, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Fatimah bint Qays, that Abu 'Amr ibn Hafs divorced her with a final (*al-battah*) divorce while he was absent in Syria. His agent sent her barley, and she was dissatisfied with it. He said: "By Allah, you have no claim on us for anything." So she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He said to her: "You have no claim on him for maintenance," and he commanded her to observe her *'iddah* in the house of Umm Sharik. Then he said: "That is a woman whom my companions frequent. Observe your *'iddah* at the house of Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is a blind man; you may take off your clothes there. When you have finished, inform me." She said: "When I finished, I mentioned to him that Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and Abu Jahm had proposed to me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'As for Abu Jahm, he does not put his staff down from his shoulder. As for Mu'awiyah, he is a poor man with no wealth. Marry Usamah ibn Zayd.'" She said: "I disliked him. Then he said: 'Marry Usamah.' So I married him, and Allah placed good in him, and I was content with him." [Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on what has been related regarding the maintenance of the divorced woman: 2/580; Muslim in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on the woman divorced three times having no maintenance, no. 1480, 2/1114; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/296-297.]

Those who did not make lodging obligatory for her argued from the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays that the Prophet ﷺ commanded her to observe her *'iddah* in the house of 'Amr ibn Umm Maktum.

But there is no proof in it, because of what is narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: "Fatimah was in a desolate place, and her safety was feared." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on whoever rejected that for Fatimah: 3/195-196; Ibn Majah: 1/655. Al-Bukhari related it as a suspended narration (*mu'allaq*): 9/479. Ibn Hajar said: it has a supporting report from the narration of Abu Usamah from Hisham from 'Urwah...]

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: "Fatimah was only moved because of the length of her tongue against her in-laws, and her tongue was sharp." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on whoever rejected that for Fatimah: 3/196, and al-Mundhiri remained silent about it.]

As for the woman in *'iddah* due to a *wat' al-shubhah* (intercourse by mistake or doubt), and the woman whose marriage was annulled due to a defect or the option of freedom (*khiyar 'itq*), she has neither lodging nor maintenance, even if she is pregnant.

[The woman in *'iddah* due to the death of her husband has no maintenance, whether pregnant or not, according to the majority of scholars. But it is narrated from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that she is entitled to maintenance from the estate if she is pregnant, until she gives birth. This is also the view of Shurayh, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i and al-Thawri.] [Note: the bracketed text is absent from "A". See al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 7/39.]

They differed regarding her lodging. al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, had two opinions on it. One is that she has no lodging, but rather she may observe her *'iddah* wherever she wishes. This is the view of 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas and 'A'ishah, also held by 'Ata' and al-Hasan, and it is the view of Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him.

The second is that she is entitled to lodging. This is the view of 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar. Malik, Sufyan al-Thawri, Ahmad and Ishaq also held it. [Note: see al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 7/41; al-Umm of al-Shafi'i: 5/208.]

Those who made lodging obligatory for her argued with what follows: Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Sa'id ibn Ishaq ibn Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, from his paternal aunt Zaynab bint Ka'b, that al-Furay'ah bint Malik ibn Sinan, who was the sister of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, informed her that she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him to let her return to her family in Bani Khudrah, because her husband had gone out in pursuit of runaway slaves of his. When he reached Tarf al-Qadum, they overtook him and killed him. So I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to let me return to my family, for my husband did not leave me in a house that he owned, nor with maintenance. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes." So I left, and when I was in the chamber or in the mosque, he called me, or the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that I be called, and I was called to him. He said: "What did you say?" She said: So I repeated to him the story I had mentioned about my husband. He said: "Remain in your house until the prescribed period (*al-kitab*) reaches its term." She said: So I observed the *'iddah* there for four months and ten days. She said: When 'Uthman was caliph, he sent for me and asked me about that, and I informed him. So he followed it and ruled by it. [Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on the widow remaining in her house until her *'iddah* ends: 2/591; Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on the widow moving: 3/198-199; al-Tirmidhi in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on where the widow should observe her *'iddah*: 4/390-391; al-Nasa'i in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on the widow remaining in her house until it ends: 6/199; Ibn Majah, no. 2031, 1/654-655; al-Darimi: 2/168 (edited by 'Abd Allah Hashim al-Yamani); Imam Ahmad: 6/370. Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. 1332, pp. 323-324. Also al-Hakim: 2/208, and al-Dhahabi concurred; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/300-301.]

Those who said this view stated: his earlier permission to al-Furay'ah to return to her family was abrogated (*mansukh*) by his later saying: "Remain in your house until the prescribed period reaches its term."

Those who did not make lodging obligatory said: he commanded her to remain in her house at the end, as a recommendation (*istihbab*), not as an obligation (*wujub*).

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And if they nurse for you﴾, meaning if they nurse your children, ﴿then give them their wages﴾ for their nursing. ﴿And confer among yourselves in kindness﴾ [so that one of you accepts from the other when he commands him with what is good]. [Note: the bracketed text is absent from "A".] al-Kisa'i said: "consult." Muqatil said: "by mutual agreement of the father and the mother on a stated wage." The address is to both spouses together, commanding them to act with kindness and with what is best, and not to intend harm.

﴿And if you disagree﴾ regarding nursing and the wage, so the husband refuses to give the woman what she is content with, and the mother refuses to nurse him, then he has no right to compel her to nurse him. Rather, he should hire another nurse for the child other than his mother. That is His saying: ﴿So another woman shall nurse for him﴾.

﴿That﴾, meaning the rulings mentioned, ﴿is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears Allah, He will remove his misdeeds from him and magnify his reward﴾.

﴿Let them dwell﴾, meaning the women you have divorced, ﴿in the same dwellings where you dwell﴾. "Min" (from) is a *ṣilah* (an extraneous particle), so the meaning is: let them dwell where you dwell. ﴿According to your means﴾, meaning your wealth and capacity. That is, if the husband is well-off, he should provide generously for her in lodging and maintenance, and if he is poor, then according to his capacity. ﴿And do not harm them﴾, meaning do not hurt them, ﴿to restrict them﴾ in their dwellings so that they are forced to leave. ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth﴾, meaning until they leave their waiting period (*'iddah*).

Know that a woman in a revocable *'iddah* is entitled from her husband to maintenance (*nafaqah*) and lodging (*sukna*) for as long as she is in the *'iddah*. By lodging we mean the cost of housing. If the house in which he divorced her belongs to the husband, he must leave and vacate the house for her for the duration of her *'iddah*. If it is rented, then the rent is the husband's obligation. If it is a loan (*'ariyah*) and the lender withdraws it, then he must rent a house for her to live in.

As for a woman in an irrevocable *'iddah* (*al-mu'taddah al-ba'innah*), whether by *khul'* (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation), by three divorces, or by *li'an* (mutual oath-cursing), she is entitled to lodging, whether she is pregnant or not, according to the majority of scholars.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "She has no lodging unless she is pregnant." This is also the view of al-Hasan, 'Ata' and al-Sha'bi.

They differed regarding her maintenance. One group held that she has no maintenance unless she is pregnant. This is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the view of al-Hasan, 'Ata' and al-Sha'bi, and al-Shafi'i and Ahmad also held it. [Note: see al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 6/507, 508.]

Others held that it is obligatory in every case. This is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, and it is the view of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. al-Thawri and the *Ashab al-Ra'y* (People of Opinion) also held it.

The apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that she is not entitled to it unless she is pregnant, because Allah the Exalted said: "And if they are pregnant, then spend on them."

The evidence from the Sunnah is what follows:

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid, client of al-Aswad ibn Sufyan, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Fatimah bint Qays, that Abu 'Amr ibn Hafs divorced her with a final (*al-battah*) divorce while he was absent in Syria. His agent sent her barley, and she was dissatisfied with it. He said: "By Allah, you have no claim on us for anything." So she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He said to her: "You have no claim on him for maintenance," and he commanded her to observe her *'iddah* in the house of Umm Sharik. Then he said: "That is a woman whom my companions frequent. Observe your *'iddah* at the house of Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is a blind man; you may take off your clothes there. When you have finished, inform me." She said: "When I finished, I mentioned to him that Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and Abu Jahm had proposed to me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'As for Abu Jahm, he does not put his staff down from his shoulder. As for Mu'awiyah, he is a poor man with no wealth. Marry Usamah ibn Zayd.'" She said: "I disliked him. Then he said: 'Marry Usamah.' So I married him, and Allah placed good in him, and I was content with him." [Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on what has been related regarding the maintenance of the divorced woman: 2/580; Muslim in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on the woman divorced three times having no maintenance, no. 1480, 2/1114; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/296-297.]

Those who did not make lodging obligatory for her argued from the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays that the Prophet ﷺ commanded her to observe her *'iddah* in the house of 'Amr ibn Umm Maktum.

But there is no proof in it, because of what is narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: "Fatimah was in a desolate place, and her safety was feared." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on whoever rejected that for Fatimah: 3/195-196; Ibn Majah: 1/655. Al-Bukhari related it as a suspended narration (*mu'allaq*): 9/479. Ibn Hajar said: it has a supporting report from the narration of Abu Usamah from Hisham from 'Urwah...]

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: "Fatimah was only moved because of the length of her tongue against her in-laws, and her tongue was sharp." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on whoever rejected that for Fatimah: 3/196, and al-Mundhiri remained silent about it.]

As for the woman in *'iddah* due to a *wat' al-shubhah* (intercourse by mistake or doubt), and the woman whose marriage was annulled due to a defect or the option of freedom (*khiyar 'itq*), she has neither lodging nor maintenance, even if she is pregnant.

[The woman in *'iddah* due to the death of her husband has no maintenance, whether pregnant or not, according to the majority of scholars. But it is narrated from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that she is entitled to maintenance from the estate if she is pregnant, until she gives birth. This is also the view of Shurayh, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i and al-Thawri.] [Note: the bracketed text is absent from "A". See al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 7/39.]

They differed regarding her lodging. al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, had two opinions on it. One is that she has no lodging, but rather she may observe her *'iddah* wherever she wishes. This is the view of 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas and 'A'ishah, also held by 'Ata' and al-Hasan, and it is the view of Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him.

The second is that she is entitled to lodging. This is the view of 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar. Malik, Sufyan al-Thawri, Ahmad and Ishaq also held it. [Note: see al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: 7/41; al-Umm of al-Shafi'i: 5/208.]

Those who made lodging obligatory for her argued with what follows: Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Sa'id ibn Ishaq ibn Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, from his paternal aunt Zaynab bint Ka'b, that al-Furay'ah bint Malik ibn Sinan, who was the sister of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, informed her that she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him to let her return to her family in Bani Khudrah, because her husband had gone out in pursuit of runaway slaves of his. When he reached Tarf al-Qadum, they overtook him and killed him. So I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to let me return to my family, for my husband did not leave me in a house that he owned, nor with maintenance. She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes." So I left, and when I was in the chamber or in the mosque, he called me, or the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that I be called, and I was called to him. He said: "What did you say?" She said: So I repeated to him the story I had mentioned about my husband. He said: "Remain in your house until the prescribed period (*al-kitab*) reaches its term." She said: So I observed the *'iddah* there for four months and ten days. She said: When 'Uthman was caliph, he sent for me and asked me about that, and I informed him. So he followed it and ruled by it. [Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on the widow remaining in her house until her *'iddah* ends: 2/591; Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on the widow moving: 3/198-199; al-Tirmidhi in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on where the widow should observe her *'iddah*: 4/390-391; al-Nasa'i in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on the widow remaining in her house until it ends: 6/199; Ibn Majah, no. 2031, 1/654-655; al-Darimi: 2/168 (edited by 'Abd Allah Hashim al-Yamani); Imam Ahmad: 6/370. Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. 1332, pp. 323-324. Also al-Hakim: 2/208, and al-Dhahabi concurred; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/300-301.]

**Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on Surah 65, verses 7–11:**

﴿Let the one of wide means spend from his wealth﴾, according to his means. ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾, from the wealth. ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it﴾ in spending, ﴿beyond what He has given it﴾, meaning, from the wealth. ﴿Allah will bring about, after hardship, ease﴾, after constraint and difficulty, wealth and abundance.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And how many a city defied the command of its Lord and His messengers﴾, meaning it disobeyed and transgressed, ﴿against the command of its Lord and His messengers﴾, that is, and the command of His messengers. ﴿So We reckoned with it a severe reckoning﴾, with close scrutiny and thorough examination. Muqatil said: He reckoned with it for its deeds in this world and then recompensed it with punishment, which is His saying: ﴿And We punished it with a terrible punishment﴾, an abhorrent, dreadful punishment, which is the punishment of the Fire. The wording of both is in the past tense, but their meaning refers to the future.

It has also been said that there is inversion (*taqdim wa ta'khir*) in the verse, and its meaning (*majaz*) is: We punished it in this world with hunger, famine, the sword and all other calamities, and We reckoned with it in the Hereafter with a severe reckoning.

﴿So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair﴾, the recompense of its affair. It has also been said: the heaviness of the outcome of its disbelief. ﴿And the outcome of its affair was loss﴾, a loss in this world and in the Hereafter.

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. So fear Allah, O people of understanding who have believed. Allah has sent down to you a reminder﴾, meaning the Qur'an.

﴿A messenger﴾ is in apposition (*badal*) to "the reminder." It has also been said: He sent down to you a Qur'an and sent a messenger. It has also been said: "with the Messenger." It has also been said: "the reminder" is the Messenger himself.

It has also been said: "a reminder" means honour (*sharaf*). Then He clarified what it is, saying: ﴿A messenger who recites to you the clear verses of Allah, to bring those who believed and did righteous deeds out of darknesses into light. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly perfected for him a provision﴾, meaning Paradise, whose bounty will never end.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 65, verse 12:

﴿Allah is the One Who created seven heavens, and of the earth the like of them [in number]﴾ [[Omitted from manuscript "b".]] ﴿The command descends among them﴾ with the revelation from the seventh heaven to the lowest earth.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: it is what He administers within them of His wondrous management, so He sends down the rain, brings forth the plants, brings the night and the day, the summer and the winter, creates the animals in their varied forms, and moves them from one state to another.

Qatadah said: in every earth of His earths and every heaven of His heavens there is a creation of His creation, a command of His command, and a decree of His decree.

﴿That you may know that Allah is over all things competent, and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾, so nothing is hidden from Him.
